title: Cross-environment progressive model gating, shadowing, and automated rollback
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary: Implement a production-grade progressive gating and rollback harness that supports canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes while respecting environment-specific constraints (networking, KMS, autoscaling, and policy). Goal is a single developer UX + API for release policies, plus environment-aware enforcement that prevents unsafe promotions and enables automatic, auditable rollback when safety gates are breached.

Scope:
- Controller component (runtime + control plane hooks) that executes rollout stages and gates across modes.
- Unified policy DSL for canary percentages, A/B splits, shadow mirroring, and multi-metric gating (latency P95, request error rate, model-quality regressions via eval hooks).
- Environment adapters: small pluggable checks for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private that enforce constraints (e.g., KMS availability, VPC egress, max burst capacity, reserved pool limits).
- Auto-rollback engine: deterministic rollback actions triggered by gate violations with configurable cool-downs and human-in-loop escalation.
- Observability & audit: tie gates to Console dashboards, traces, token-level cost attribution, and append audit events for each promotion/rollback for compliance.
- API/Console controls: per-release preview, manual override, and staged resume.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Canaries can be declared in the API and executed across modes with the same policy DSL; parity tests show policy outcomes are equivalent for identical constraints in Hosted and Dedicated (within environment limits).
- Automatic rollback fires and completes within SLA when gate thresholds exceeded in >=2 independent checks (latency and error rate) for a canary within 5 minutes.
- Shadowing pipeline supports live traffic mirroring to Dedicated/Private variants without impacting production latencies (less than 2% added tail latency on average).
- End-to-end audit trail and rollout timeline visible in Console for every rollout; audit export to customer S3/Drive for Private installs.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- "Policy first" vs "Orchestration-first": we chose policy-first (DSL) so higher-level product rules can be expressed and validated before executing. This increases validation complexity but reduces ad-hoc orchestration drift across environments.
- Conservative defaults for Private installs: default to manual promotion unless customer enables automated rollouts (opt-in) because on-prem constraints (no centralized KMS/HSM) and offline networks increase risk.
- Shadow traffic bandwidth: for Dedicated and Private, we limit mirror sampling by default to avoid burst billing; provide explicit sample controls in policy DSL.
- Fallback behavior: prefer model variant fallback (smaller/FP16/quantized) over full rollback when the degradation is only resource-related (e.g., OOM) and model quality remains acceptable.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Policy DSL schema + validation library (server and Console) — implement feature flags for staged rollout.
2) Environment adapters and capability registry (KMS, egress, burst capacity, quota APIs).
3) Controller: execution engine with state machine for canary percentages, timers, and rollback triggers.
4) Auto-rollback heuristics and escalation paths—hook into Alerting and PagerDuty runbooks.
5) Console integration: rollout view, manual controls, and audit timeline.
6) E2E tests across hosted/dedicated/private in staging; chaos tests for network partitions and capacity events.

Dependencies: ["ENG-4027","ENG-8451","ENG-9274"]

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Private deployment variability (custom networking/KMS) may produce false-positives in automated gates. Mitigation: add preflight capability checks and require manual opt-in for auto-rollback on Private.
- Risk: Shadow traffic may increase costs or leak PII. Mitigation: provide PII scrubbers and cost-limited shadow sampling by default.

Rollout plan: alpha with internal Redwood services (2 weeks), closed beta with 3 customers on Dedicated (4 weeks), gated availability for Private with opt-in (6 weeks). Metrics to track: number of rollouts, rollback rate, mean time to rollback, shadow sampling overhead, customer opt-ins for auto-rollback.

Open questions:
- Should A/B metric weighting support custom statistical tests per customer or just default t-test/chi-square? (Design to decide during implementation).
- How to represent cross-mode cost accounting for shadow traffic in billing dashboards? (PM/Finance to define mapping).
